moves.note: Cap single name, favor broad index

plan: Sell all SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure and stop losses.
Sell METU, PLTU, and MSFU to further reduce leveraged exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to cap single name concentration.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a potential ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and high-beta names. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns.

plan: Trim SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure and manage stop losses.
Trim METU, PLTU, and MSFU to reduce overall leveraged exposure.
Buy TSM at 4% to add a high-scoring, quality long setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some tech exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth by reducing leverage and adding quality tech. It aims for a moderate risk profile with controlled exposure to leveraged ETFs. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to increase leveraged ETF exposure, despite being below stop.
Add to METU, PLTU, and MSFU to further increase leveraged exposure.
Buy TSM at 6% to concentrate in a high-scoring long setup.
This plan aggressively seeks growth through increased leverage and concentration.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth by significantly increasing leveraged exposure and concentration. It carries substantially higher drawdown risk, including daily decay of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell all SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure and stop losses.
Sell METU, PLTU, and MSFU to reduce all leveraged exposure.
Add to QQQI to increase allocation to income-focused ETFs.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly yield by rotating into income and broad index ETFs. It aims for low drawdown and reliable distributions, but NAV can still fall. This is for income, not a savings account.
